title: The 88 Keys trio with Josh Johnson in the fifties
summary: He played the 88 Keys for an Italian owner named Martin as a trio with Josh Johnson and Clayborn Graves, into the sixties.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well,where did you play mostly in the fifties?
Fifties.
When -- did you go back to Milton's or--
No, I never went back to Milton's.
How about 88 Keys --
I was out at the 88 Keys.
What, in the fifties.
Yeah, yeah. And Josh Johnson was playing piano.
Who else was with you? Or was it just the two of you?
Just the two of us.
All through the fifties, just you and Josh?
Just Josh and I, that's all I can remember. Oh, and Clayborn Graves.
On saxophone.
Yes, tenor saxophone.
Just the trio.
Trio, yes. And we was working for a fine man by the name of Martin, I don't know his last name. Italian guy.
At the 88 Keys.
Yeah, 88 Keys.

Well, you were out there for a long time because you introduced me to Mr. Martin shortly after I got to Kansas City, which was in late 1961, and I went out to hear you out at the 88 Keys and you introduced me to him, so you were there into the sixties I know.
Yeah.
And I remember you and Josh used to drive me back to my hotel when I first came --
Really right. After (inaudible).
Yeah, after the gig, you remember that big old car of Josh's?
Sure.
And God rest his soul. Yeah.
He was a fine guy.
